items.title: Hal Espinosa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 20, 2024
items.q: He was the other name, entertainer, that I played when I was 17.

ctx.x: I guess my point is the big band era had faded out for the most part. What were your aspirations and how did you see that playing a trumpet could be a career?

Well you know at that time I never thought of playing the trumpet as a career. It was just a fun thing to do and it became more fun as I got better naturally, and then finally I got to be on first chair in high school. And I was really into sports except I’m not tall and I’m not big heavy wise, and I loved baseball, basketball, football and I was good at it in junior © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

high school but when I got to high school all these kids that were my size or a couple of inches taller just grew like a foot taller. So finally I, you know the fact that I was practicing a lot a couple of guys from the high school band went to Arizona State on scholarships, and they’d come back and tell me, “Harold, you’ve got to audition for a scholarship.” So I thought why not, I’ll do that. So two of us went over and I got a scholarship. So at that time I got free tuition plus $100 for the year. You know to…
